meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the D-400 unit
meta.scope: From the feed battery limit (upstream of XV-408) through E-400 (both sides, from XV-409), D-400 with PSV-400 and the N₂ blanket, to the vapour battery limit (downstream of HV-421) and the liquid battery limit (downstream of HV-411), including utilities (hot oil, N₂, instrument air).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
HV-401 feed block valve gate drops (fails closed)
FCV-400 shut (FIC-400 fault, positioner or instrument-air failure: fail closed)
XV-408 closes spuriously
supply pump trips upstream
N1.cons: Production stops. E-400 tubes hold stagnant feed while hot oil still flows: the feed heats toward the hot-oil temperature, vaporises and, if blocked in, over-pressures the tube side. D-400 level and pressure fall toward the N2 blanket.

N1.causes:
Supply pressure falls (upstream pump loses head) until FCV-400 runs out of travel
FT-400 reads high (drift, plugged impulse line)
FCV-400 stiction after packing work
HV-401 partly closed
N1.cons: Lower throughput. At low flow the E-400 outlet runs hotter for the same oil, TIC-401 gain and dead time grow and the loop cycles; flow swings reach the drum as vapour-rate swings.

N1.causes:
FCV-400 fails wide open (positioner fault, FIC-400 in MAN at a high output)
FT-400 reads low
set point entered too high
globe bypass HV-403 opened with FCV-400 in service
N1.cons: E-400 cannot heat the extra feed (hot feed colder, less vapour per tonne) while the total vapour and liquid rates rise well above design (see dynamic check): level rises, mesh-pad overload and carry-over, header and downstream receiver overloaded.

N1.dev: Back-flow from E-400 and D-400 toward the supply
N1.causes:
Supply pump stops with D-400 at pressure and XV-408 open
supply pressure below drum pressure during start-up
N1.cons: Hot, light hydrocarbon flows back into the supply line and tank; flashing and hammer in the supply line; D-400 inventory lost.

N1.dev: Feed line or E-400 tubes over-pressured
N1.causes:
FCV-400, HV-403 and HV-401 closed with the supply pump running (shut-off 650 kPa g)
liquid blocked in between XV-408 and FCV-400 and heated by hot oil
N1.cons: Shut-off head alone is within the line rating, but blocked-in liquid heated by hot oil rises in pressure without limit: flange leak or tube rupture, release and fire.

N1.causes:
Upstream pump losing head
low supply-tank level
plugged strainer
N1.cons: FCV-400 opens to hold the flow and loses its margin unseen; lower pressure in E-400 lowers the bubble point of the hot feed (vapour ahead of FCV-400).

N1.causes:
Feed from a sun-heated tank
upstream cooler out of service
N1.cons: E-400 needs less duty (TCV-401 closes); feed nearer its bubble point in the supply line: upstream pump cavitation.

N1.causes: Tank switch to a lighter feed (butane toward 45 wt%)
N1.cons: More vapour and higher drum pressure demand on PCV-420; liquid product C4 above the 28 wt% spec sent downstream.

N1.causes: Tank switch to a heavier feed (butane toward 25 wt%)
N1.cons: Less vapour, more liquid; vapour carries more C6 so AI-420 falls toward its 75 wt% spec; LCV-400 opens further.

N1.causes: Water carried from tank bottoms after a tank switch
N1.cons: Water boils in E-400 and D-400 (pressure surges), collects in the drum bottom and goes to the downstream unit; ice or hydrate in the let-down valve at low temperature; corrosion.

N1.causes:
Orifice plate damaged
impulse line leak or plugged
wrong range after calibration
N1.cons: FIC-400 holds the wrong flow; the true feed rate is unknown; balances do not close and faults are misread.

recs.text: Interlock the hot oil to the feed: close XV-409 on low-low feed flow (an element independent of FT-400) and whenever XV-408 closes, so E-400 is never heated with the tube side blocked in or stagnant.
Fit a thermal relief valve on the E-400 tube side (between XV-408 and FCV-400), sized for blocked-in liquid heated by hot oil at 180 °C, discharging to a closed system.
Add a check valve in the feed line downstream of XV-408 so D-400 and E-400 cannot flow back into the supply when the supply pump stops.
Add a feed supply pressure indicator with low alarm upstream of FCV-400 and a FIC-400 output-high alarm, so loss of supply head is seen before FCV-400 runs out of travel.
Limit the feed with FCV-400 wide open (travel stop or restriction orifice), or show that D-400, the mesh pad, PCV-420 and the downstream receiver handle that flow.
Run the Rev B cascades (TIC-401 → FIC-405, LIC-400 → FIC-410) as the normal configuration; state the minimum stable feed rate for TIC-401 in the start-up procedure.
Sample the feed at every tank switch and the products each shift; add a flat-line (frozen signal) alarm on AI-410 and AI-420.
Draw water from the feed tank before a switch and check the feed for free water; include a D-400 low-point water check in the rounds.
Add a DCS material balance (FT-400 against FI-410 + FI-420) with a deviation alarm, to reveal meter errors and a passing PSV-400.
